newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares snap losing streak, end firm.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares snap losing streak, end firm.

text.p: Breaking a five session losing run, Chilean blue chips closed firm on bargain hunting by brokers trading their own accounts, said dealers.
The rally is expected to continue at Friday's opening, they said.
"People think that in future prices will not be near the low levels they have reached today," said one trader.
The selective index ended up 0.44 percent at 88.33 points. The general index gained 0.28 percent to 4,882.5 points amid volume of 10.6 billion pesos.
The low turnover reflected the absence of institutional investors including the heavyweight pension funds, said dealers.
The funds, which moved into the market last year to push the IPSA idex to a year-end close over 100 points, are not expected to help the beleaguered bolsa again this year, said daelers.
"The funds are staying on the sidelines and are not likely to rescue the market again," said one dealer.
Winners included pension fund manager Provida , up 2.24 percent at 7,750 pesos, telecoms company Telex, up 2.15 percent 950 pesos and power utility Enersis which rose 1.93 percent to 224-3/4 pesos.
Losers included salmon company Mainstream, down 6.98 percent at 30 pesos and forestry firm Infodema which lost 4.55 percent to 21 pesos.
